title: AI-AUGMENTED HAZARD DETECTION AND AVOIDANCE FOR THE L4 ENCELADUS LANDER - EXPRO+
description: ObjectivesAssess the feasibility of using physics-based granular dynamics simulation to model the formation of cryovolcanic terrains on Enceladus and derive insights into surface compactness. Develop a proof-of-concept ML model for inferring snow/ice geophysicalproperties (e.g., density, snow water equivalent) by correlating terrestrial in-situ scientific data with satellite remote sensing observations. Initiate the adaptation of classical, optimization-based HDA frameworks to integrate AIderived geophysical safety maps, establishing a baseline for a future hybrid HDA architecture. Conduct an extensive performance and resource consumption benchmark of key AI and HDA software components on representative space-grade hardware, establishing the trade-space between algorithmic capability and on-board computational budgetDescriptionThe ESA Voyage 2050 L4 mission to Enceladus requires an autonomous landing in the South Polar Terrain to achieve its core astrobiological objectives. This environment presents unique challenges that transcend classical HDA capabilities. Landing hazardsare not only geometric (e.g., slopes, rocks), but also geophysical. Due to the unknown load-bearing capacity of cryovolcanic surface deposits, landing sites can appear perfectly flat and clear of hazards and yet be catastrophically unsafe. Classical existing Hazard Detection and Avoidance (HDA) frameworks targeting Moon and Mars, are highly mature for geometric hazard assessment but are not designed to infer subsurface geophysical properties from remote sensing data. This activity shall address this critical technology gap by investigating the integration of AI/ML-based geophysicalinference into a proven HDA decision-making architecture. Additionally, the severe power and computational constraints of a solar-powered missionto Saturn imposea hard limit on the complexity of on-board AI. It is currently unknown what level of "intelligence" is achievable within a realistic resource budget. This activity shall perform the foundational trade-off analysis required to inform mission designers of the necessary hardware and power provisions for a reliable and capable AI-augmented HDA system

title: AI-REACT - ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE READINESS EVALUATION AND ASSESSMENT FOR EARTH SCIENCE CHALLENGES AND OPPORTUNITIES - EXPRO PLUS
description: Strategic assessment activity to evaluate the readiness of artificial intelligence to support Earth system science and future ESA Earth Observation missions. The activity will assess AI approaches across the EO Science Strategy and its Overarching Science Themes,with a focus on identifying where AI is already delivering credible scientific value, where important scientific and technical gapsremain, and where maturity is sufficient to support mission-facing tasks such as geophysical observables retrieval development, observation requirement definition, observing-system analysis, and science-gap identification. It will build a structured evidence base, assess scientific rigour and mission relevance, and develop an AI readiness framework aligned with ESA readiness principles, leadingto a roadmap for FutureEO investments and follow-on actions. A core outcome of the study is a decision-ready assessment of where AIcan credibly strengthen future EO mission science and planning, and where further evidence or development is still required.

title: NAVISP-EL1-131-CHIP SCALE OPTICAL ATOMIC CLOCK FOR PNT APPLICATIONS EXPRO+ REISSUE OF (1-13610)
description: Development of a compact optical atomic clock module (physics package) for PNT applications. The activity will design, manufacture,and test an Engineering Model (EM) of a chip-scale optical clock exploiting an atomic optical transition to achieve 10 improved stability (target timing drift 10-30 ns/day) versus existing microwave clocks. The clock will provide a stabilized optical frequencyoutput in a low-power (< 5 W), compact device. Tasks include detailed thermo-mechanical design for robust operation in harsh environments, definition of low-power control electronics requirements and autonomous operation algorithms, assembly of the optical clock physics package, and development of Electrical Ground Support Equipment (EGSE) to control and test the EM. The EM will undergo performance verification in ambient and thermal conditions to demonstrate its stability, targeting TRL 4-5 and paving the way for future space-qualified ultra-stable timing solutions for navigation and timing systems.

title: COMPATIBILITY VALIDATION TESTBED OF THE OPTICAL HEAD AND ITS CONTROL OF OPTICAL COMMUNICATION TERMINALS (ARTES 4.0 SL SPL 5H.015)
description: Objective: The objective of this activity is to develop a testbed that will test the interoperability between different suppliers of optical communication terminals. Thisshall include free-space optics testing to evaluate the pointing, acquisition, and tracking performance.TargetedImprovements:To enable independent on-ground validation of optical communication terminal interoperability ina facility located in ESA member states.Description: With an increasing number of constellations considering the use of optical inter satellite links and cross-atmospheric links, it is important to test, validateand ultimately certify the interoperability between different laser terminals manufactured by multiple suppliers.This activity will develop the capability of enabling independent interoperability validation between various laser communication terminals. The focus willbe on pointing, acquisition and tracking performance validation for both intersatellite and cross-atmospheric optical links. The developed testbed shallenable the performancevalidation of the terminal optical head in free space, and the compatibility validation of the pointing, acquisition and trackingsequence implemented by optical terminal (both space and ground) suppliers. The testbed will enable the validation to be carried out between two terminalsunder test from different suppliers and shall be accessible to all the ESA member states industries.Procurement Policy: C(1) = Activity restricted to non-prime contractors (incl. SMEs).
